# IUT audit ledger

This file records what was actually checked in this workspace. It is a scope
ledger, not a claim that IUT has been proved or refuted. Statuses mean:

- **proved**: Lean checked the statement without an IUT-specific premise being
  hidden in the proof;
- **interface**: Lean checked a theorem after a record/certificate containing
  the mathematical content was supplied;
- **claim only**: the code states the intended theorem or vocabulary, but does
  not prove its IUT-specific existence/construction;
- **not checked**: no local verification yet.

## 2026-08-07 polymorphic quotient and Tate-boundary batch

The reusable algebra layer now has three deliberately polymorphic modules:
`Foundations/Algebra/CyclicQuotient.lean` abstracts the `g^Z` quotient over
any commutative group and proves representative, power, descent, and
surjectivity laws; `FiniteCyclicQuotient.lean` abstracts finite additive
quotients over any additive commutative group and specializes the integer
kernel certificate; `FiniteCyclicQuotientTransport.lean` transports such
quotients through a commuting carrier/label square.  These APIs are intended
for reuse by Kummer packets, prime strips, and theta links, so no separate
copy of the same quotient proof is introduced for each carrier.

`Foundations/Geometry/TatePointQuotientBoundary.lean` retains only the
source-faithful point comparison record, its injectivity/surjectivity and

coordinate comparison into `CurveIndexedTateUniformization`.  Redundant
q-unit wrapper lemmas were removed; the already proved deck quotient module is
used directly.  `IUTI/InitialTheta/TateComparisonBoundary.lean` and
`SourceLocalTateBoundary.lean` compose these records with dependent
finite-place/q data and expose finite-level transport projections.

## 2026-08-07 concrete finite Theorem 3.11 model batch

`LeanFormal/IUT/IUTIII/Theorem311/ConcreteFiniteModel.lean` ports the useful
finite part of the public Stage-1 construction onto the project's own proved
C-stage carrier.  Its `ProcessionChoice` has two `ZMod l` translation
coordinates and one `Nat` upper-semi level.  The file proves the identity,
composition, inverse, cancellation, and mutual-commutation laws for the first
two actions; reflexive/transitive reachability for all three layers; and the
invariance/monotonicity of the concrete theta log-volume.  It also constructs
the singleton possible-image correspondence, proves its upper-semi law, and
reuses the actual finite Kummer quotient, compatible roots, q-deck action, and
positive theta-packet determinant/log-volume identities.

The standalone compile log is
`logs/lean/concrete-theorem311-finite-model-standalone-r4.log`; the production
build is `logs/lean/concrete-theorem311-finite-model-project-20260807.log`
(`3884/3884`, zero diagnostics).  The expanded endpoint audit is recorded in
`logs/lean/axioms-20260807-073811/axiom_audit.stdout.log` through
`logs/lean/concrete-theorem311-finite-model-axiom-boundary-20260807-r2.log`.
The new declarations use only the standard `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and
`Quot.sound` foundations; the permitted production `sorryAx` remains solely
`LeanFormal.IUT.theorem311_produces_stepXI_contract`.  The custom declaration
scan remains zero.

This is an explicitly labelled finite model boundary, not a proof of the
paper's arbitrary procession of D-prime-strips, distinct Hodge theaters,
source log-Kummer correspondence, or the full multiradial algorithm.  In
particular it does not discharge `(Ind1)`, `(Ind2)`, `(Ind3)` in the source
setting and does not remove the Step-XI contract boundary.  It is useful as a
reusable test carrier for those future source-faithful constructions without
duplicating quotient/action code.

## Complete author-site corpus and citation map

The author-site crawl now lives under `papers/motizuki_corpus/`. It fetched the
eight entry pages (`papers-japanese.html`, `top-japanese.html`, CV, students,
thoughts, news, research, and travel), found 263 unique PDF links, and saved
262 files with SHA-256 hashes. One external link,
`~yuichiro/absolute_anabelian_cuspidalizations.pdf`, returned a confirmed 404
and is retained as a missing row in `pdfs.csv`; it is not silently omitted.
The downloaded corpus is about 644 MB and includes papers, comments, LaTeX
versions, lecture notes, and dated talk/slide PDFs linked from the site.

The bundled PDF workflow extracted 262 PDFs into `papers/motizuki_corpus/text/`
(8197 pages, about 14.8 million characters). The citation pass produced:

- `citation_edges.tsv`: 478 resolved label-to-file candidate edges;
- `reference_snippets.tsv`: 1449 bibliography snippets for manual review;
- `unresolved_reference_labels.tsv`: 112 unresolved historical labels;
- `DEPENDENCY_LAYERS.md`: the source-backed bottom-up layer plan.

The edges are evidence for reading order, not a proof of mathematical
dependency. In particular, the Tan introduction explicitly says to treat
anabelian/Frobenioid theory as prior material, read `EtTh` Sections 1--2, then
IUT I/II, and read IUT III carefully; IUT IV Section 1 can be read alongside
IUT III. This is now the basis for the Lean directory order.

## What the original papers require

1. **IUT I-II (prerequisites):** initial Theta data, distinct Hodge-theater
   histories, prime strips, Hodge-Arakelov theta evaluation, Gaussian/LGP
   monoids, and the Kummer/coric infrastructure. No local Lean project here
   constructs these objects from an elliptic curve and its number field.
2. **IUT III, Theorem 3.11:** a multiradial output consisting of tensor packets
   of log-shells, splitting monoids, and labelled copies of `F_mod`, with
   `(Ind1)`, `(Ind2)`, `(Ind3)` and the stated Kummer/link compatibilities.
3. **IUT III, Corollary 3.12:** the disputed final passage is explicit in the
   proof, especially PDF pages 174--184 (printed pp. 174--184):
   `IPL` links the output to the q-pilot prime strip; `SHE` says the output is
   expressible in the fixed 1-column arithmetic holomorphic structure;
   `APT` justifies the algorithmic transport; the holomorphic hull and
   log-volume then yield `-|log(q)| in R_{<= -|log(Theta)|}`. This is the
   logical wall. It is not just a numerical `j^2` calculation.
4. **IUT IV:** its abstract theorem (PDF pp. 1--3) and the Section 1/2
   estimates use IUT III Corollary 3.12 (e.g. the explicit final step on PDF
   p. 31 and the discussion beginning p. 40). Thus an IUT IV numerical proof
   cannot close the earlier wall by itself.

The LANA interim report (`papers/LANA_report_202607.pdf`, extracted in
`tmp/pdfs/lana.txt`) independently describes the same remaining obligation:
the q-pilot-native construction must be compatible with the multiradial/
Kummer construction after Ind1--3; its abstract (PDF p. 1) says the proof has
not been reconstructed, and pp. 4--6 call this diagram-commutativity/
identity issue the ``wall``. This is a status report, not a verdict.

## Local Lean checks

### Minimal diagnostic model (this workspace)

| file | status | checked fact | limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| `LeanFormal/IUTDispute.lean` | **proved** | In a same ordered space, monotonicity makes the comparison tautological; with `q < 0`, `factor > 1`, `theta = factor*q`, a tight-hull premise `q <= hull <= theta` is inconsistent; a slack witness satisfies the receiver/common-container shape while violating tightness. | This is an order-theoretic diagnostic. It does not define Hodge theaters, Kummer maps, or the source of the premises. |
| `LeanFormal/Archive/AnalysisExercise/Basic.lean` | **archived** (separate analysis exercise) | A real-analysis limit problem is fully checked and is unrelated to IUT. | It is outside the production entry point and must not be counted as IUT progress. |

The diagnostic therefore supports only: **the dispute is a missing/contested
identification or compatibility premise, not an arithmetic contradiction in the
abstract inequality.** It does not decide which side is mathematically right.

### Project hierarchy and proof boundary

The local project is now organized into deep, source-oriented modules rather
than one flat `IUT` directory. `LeanFormal/IUT/Project.lean` is the aggregate
entry point. The current hierarchy is:

- `Audit`: source hashes, status vocabulary, and obligation metadata;
- `Foundations/Arithmetic`, `Theta`, `Coordinates`, and `Volumes`: standard
  algebra, the square-exponent theta kernel and finite square-sum normalization, labelled real coordinates, and
  finite weighted-average lemmas;
- `IUTI/InitialTheta`, `IUTI/HodgeTheater`, `IUTII/Frobenioid`, and
  `IUTII/Kummer`:
  source obligations for the IUT I--II constructions;
- `Theorem311/Output` and `Theorem311/Indeterminacy/Ind1--Ind3`:
  Theorem 3.11 obligations plus the generic `Setoid`/`Quotient` transport
  kernel;
- `Corollary312/StepXI/IPL`, `SHE`, `APT`, and
  `HolomorphicHull/Volume`, `FiniteCertificateBridge`: the exact disputed wall;
- `ABCBridge/Statement`, `ABCBridge/UnprovedTarget`, and `ABCBridge/Bridge`: the standard ABC
  proposition, its explicit unfinished proof target, and the eventual bridge.

The following distinction is enforced in code:

source-oriented dependency tree are under `Audit/Diagnostics`; they are
quarantined experiments and are not imported by `Project.lean`. This prevents
an old placeholder interface from silently becoming a dependency of the new
formalization.

These repositories are complementary rather than independent completed proofs:
the closest source-facing implementation is promachina's, the most explicit
axioms/deferral ledger is Takkun's, iut4-sec1 covers elementary downstream
arithmetic, and the other two are scaffolds or unrelated proven mathematics.
The four decisions used below are `direct-proof`, `migrated-proof`,
`interface-only`, and `excluded`; packaging or regression declarations are not
counted as mathematical progress.

## Outstanding obligations (the checklist to update)

The following must become concrete Lean definitions and proofs before anyone
can claim that the wall has been crossed:

- Construct the actual IUT I initial Theta data and distinct Hodge-theater
  histories from the stated number field/elliptic-curve hypotheses.
- Construct the IUT I-II prime strips, Hodge-Arakelov evaluation, theta/LGP
  monoids, mono-theta cyclotomic rigidity, and the vertical log-Kummer
  correspondence; do not replace them by an arbitrary record with the same
  field names.
- Construct Theorem 3.11's multiradial algorithm and prove its Ind1/Ind2
  quotient and Ind3 upper-semi compatibility from that construction.
- Prove the horizontal/vertical compatibility needed to transport the output
  into the 1-column while preserving the q-pilot's fixed arithmetic-holomorphic
  condition (the paper's `SHE` and `APT`).
- Define the holomorphic hull, determinant/tensor normalization, and local/global
  log-volume maps and prove the comparison that gives membership in
  `R_{<= -|log(Theta)|}`.
- Only after those items, formalize IUT IV's explicit estimates and its
  Diophantine corollaries.

Until these boxes are discharged, the defensible conclusion is: **the papers
state a complete claimed argument, but the disputed compatibility remains an
unverified prerequisite; the available Lean code demonstrates conditional
corridors and diagnostics, not a resolution of the controversy.**

## 2026-11-05 discriminant-route facts for Aoc2 = S (S2571)

Scope: `tmp/sheaf/xif/paper/S2571DiscriminantPrimitiveActual.lean` (EXIT=0,
axioms trio only). Status: **proved** for the reduction and the instance bank;
**claim only / open** for `S ⊆ Aoc2`.

- Mathlib v4.32.2 has no instance that `ℚ` is a fraction ring of the
  localization `ℤ[1/c]`. Working route: `IsLocalization.lift` from `ℤ → ℚ`
  (+ `lift_comp`) for `Algebra R ℚ`, then
  `IsFractionRing.isFractionRing_of_isDomain_of_isLocalization`, and
  `isIntegrallyClosed_of_isLocalization` for integral closedness.
- Instance-search pitfall (reproducible): if `c : ℤ` is a plain `def` and
  `R := Localization (Submonoid.powers c)`, then
  `IsLocalization (Submonoid.powers (Cden : ℤ)) R` does **not** synthesize —
  typeclass unification does not unfold the `def` `c`. Using the `abbrev`
  `M := Submonoid.powers c` (S2565) fixes it.
- Second pitfall: for `L = SplittingField f`, the derived instances
  `SplittingField.instSMulOfIsScalarTower` for `SMul ℚ L` / `SMul R L` are not
  definitionally `Algebra.toSMul`, so `IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq'` (whose
  conclusion is phrased with `Algebra.toSMul`) fails to apply. Declaring
  `local instance : SMul _ _ := Algebra.toSMul` for the Z/R/ℚ actions (as S2565
  does) makes all tower and `Algebra.smul_def` rewrites go through.
- Mathematics: with K = ℚ, `Algebra.discr_mul_isIntegral_mem_adjoin` gives
  `discr ℚ B.basis • z ∈ R[B.gen]` for every z integral over R; a unit
  discriminant δ ∈ Rˣ therefore yields `z ∈ R[B.gen]`, which is the reduction
  implemented here. The hypothesis is not discharged: HZc2 is a scalar multiple
  of the image of `S1720H = S1687H * (X^2 + 1)` (S2481HZ_map_rat) and is
  reducible, so a root of HZc2 has minimal polynomial of degree at most 6 and
  cannot be a primitive element of `L/ℚ`; for an abstract primitive element the
  unit-discriminant condition is exactly order maximality at the primes outside
  Cden, i.e. the statement being proved. No unconditional `S ⊆ Aoc2` is
  claimed.

## 2026-11-05 index-route facts for Aoc2 = S (S2575)

Scope: `tmp/sheaf/xif/paper/S2575IndexOrderMaximalityActual.lean` (521 lines,
EXIT=0, olean built; all 43 `#print axioms` are the trio
[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]). Status: **proved** for the lattice /
index / discriminant reduction; **open** for `S <= Aoc2`.

- Proved unconditionally: `R = Z[1/Cden]` is Dedekind and a principal ideal
  ring; `Algebra R Q`, `IsFractionRing R Q`, `IsScalarTower R Q L`;
  `Module.Finite R S`; `Module.Free`/`Module.Projective` for `Aoc2` and
  `S`; the rank equality `finrank R Aoc2 = finrank R S = finrank Q L`; the
  inclusion `Aoc2 <= Ssub := range (S -> L)`.
- For free bases `basisA` (Aoc2) and `basisS` (S), the coordinate matrix
  `indexMatrix` of the inclusion satisfies
  `discr Q (algebraMap Aoc2 o basisA) = (algebraMap R Q indexMatrix.det)^2 *
  discr Q (algebraMap S o basisS)` (`discr_indexMatrix_relation`).
- Exact equivalence proved: `OrderIsMaximal <-> IsUnit indexMatrix.det` and
  `OrderIsMaximal <-> IndexIdeal = top` with `IndexIdeal := span
  {indexMatrix.det}`; hence `IndexIsUnitGoal -> IsIntegrallyClosed Aoc2`.
- Open input `IndexIsUnitGoal`: the index `[S : Aoc2]` is the unit ideal of
  `R = Z[1/Cden]` (every prime factor of the integer index divides `Cden`).
  Mathlib v4.32.2 has no conductor / index-divisibility theorem for the
  multi-generated order `Z[1/Cden][all HZc2 roots]`; the S2564 unit
  discriminant of the octic does not bound this index because `HZc2` is
  reducible and no root is a primitive element of `L` (see the S2571 entry).
  No unconditional `S <= Aoc2` or `IsIntegrallyClosed Aoc2` is claimed.
- Consumer `tmp/sheaf/xif/paper/_S2575Consumer.lean` imports the built olean
  and restates the equivalences, the reduction, the discriminant relation, the
  rank equality, inclusion and free/projective instances; EXIT=0, axioms trio.

## 2026-11-06 — S2573 f model obstruction; localized correction (ACTUAL plan)

- **Obstruction (recorded, not silently dropped).** `S2573ResidueDataObligations.f`
  asks for a monic model in `(O_{F'})[X]` of a nonzero `F'`-multiple of
  `S2057Psi5F`, with leading coefficient normalized to one.  The actual
  integer model has leading coefficient `Lc = 2^36 * 5 = 343597383680` and
  constant coefficient `5^18 = 3814697265625` (S2132Psi5Z).  Hence the monic
  scalar normalization over `F'` is `f = (1/(2^36*5)) * S2132Psi5Z`; its
  constant coefficient is `5^17 / 2^36`, which is not in `O_{F'}` because
  `2` is a nonunit of `O_{F'}` (norm argument; exact piece
  `¬ IsUnit (2 : O_{F'})` is kernel-proved in probe, no sorry).  Equivalently
  the coefficient comparison gives `2^36 * f.coeff 0 = 5^17`, forcing `2` to
  be a unit, contradiction.  Therefore the original monic `f` datum is
  **uninhabitable**; S2573/S2470/S2530 monic residue data cannot be closed in
  this form.  The earlier GAP-TABLE line “monic model obstructed 5^17/2^36”
  is this same obstruction.
- **Localized correction (actual first segment).**
  `tmp/sheaf/xif/paper/S2574LocalizedModelActual.lean` inverts the leading
  coefficient: `R := O_{F'}[1/(2^36*5)]`, `Lc := 343597383680`, and defines
  `f : R[X] := C (invSelf Lc) * S2132Psi5Z.map (Z -> R)`.  It proves
  `f_coeff_12 = 1`, `f_natDegree = 12`, and `f_monic`; EXIT=0, olean
  191712 B, src SHA `AB3DF812F966F2EF3B922B01CF05C41C50D824B98BC11162501BB1A26D3B1F87`,
  olean SHA `6573B5A353FDE1829E794DBC093E238112AEF0709F496AEEA56F47D4E5398C49`.
  This is the correct localized model; it is not the original S2573 datum.
- **Plan update.** Replace the S2573/S2470 monic datum by localized residue
  data over `R = O_{F'}[1/Lc]` (or the stronger `S = O_{F'}[1/Cden]` used by
  `S2574LocalizedP12Actual.lean`):
  1. use `S2574LocalizedModelActual.f`/`f_monic` as the monic model;
  2. define the localized residue ideal `p` over 613 and prime `P` above it in
     the localized five-division algebra; keep `fbar` irreducible degree 12
     from F613/S2572 and root-set cardinality as separate conditions;
  3. transport the Dedekind/Frobenius 12-cycle theorem only over localized
     rings, not over `O_{F'}`;
  4. do not re-assert `S2573ResidueDataObligations` or `S2470ActualResidueData`
     over `O_{F'}`; mark them BLOCKED with this obstruction.
  `S2574LocalizedP12Actual.lean` (source SHA `8E5F8E9578BCAAE14DC5EF2782B474922A8DB631E2D39A2CA01F288918463FC5`)
  is the stronger localized `S = O_{F'}[1/Cden]` version; olean not yet
  confirmed at ledger time, so it is plan input, not an ACTUAL claim.
- Status: obstruction recorded; localized model actual; localized residue
  assembly and transport remain open.  No fake monic model over `O_{F'}`.

## 2026-11-06 — CRITICAL CORRECTION: sourceThetaPilotPoint is a constant log-thetaValueAt point; gauss degree unconditional

- Definition (actual):
  `sourceThetaPilotPoint v R n j = fun _ => thetaImageValue R n j`
  (`LeanFormal/IUT/IUTIII/Corollary312/StepXI/HolomorphicHull/SourceImageHull.lean:199-203`).
- `thetaImageValue R n j = R.posRealAction (Multiplicative.ofAdd (Real.log (I.thetaValueAt (n.1 : Int) 0 j)))`
  by `thetaImageValue_eq` (rfl; same file :177-182).
  Hence `sourceThetaPilotPoint` is definitionally the **constant global point
  of the log thetaValueAt**, not merely a generic constant witness.
- The actual degree theorem
  `sourceLocalLogDegree_thetaPilotPoint_gauss`
  (`CardHullRealGeneratorNonpositivity.lean:301-...`) is **unconditional**:
  it has no `hdeg` premise and proves
  `sourceLocalLogDegree v (sourceThetaPilotPoint v R n j)
    = card(SourceVolumeIndex l) * (gaussExponent j.toNat * log q_0)`.
- **P4/P5 must anchor here.** The earlier P4 route through a pointwise
  degree-faithfulness hypothesis `hdeg` (e.g. `P4SourceLogDegreeCandidate_eq`
  in S2593) is **obsolete** and must not be used as the P4/P5 justification.
  P4/P5 dictionary wiring should use this unconditional gauss formula.
- Status label: **critical correction; prior hdeg route superseded**.

## 2026-11-06 — MAJOR: fixed scaling/degreeBound makes P4 false; lambda may be triple-dependent

- **P4 is FALSE under fixed scaling/degreeBound.** For a fixed scaling and fixed
  degree bound, the P4 region volume is constant, while the arithmetic weight
  is unbounded over ABC triples. Hence the inequality
  `arithmeticWeight ≤ regionVolume + constant` cannot hold uniformly; the
  frozen fixed-scaling P4 target is refuted, not merely unproved.
- **The paper's lambda may be triple-dependent.** If the paper's λ depends on
  the triple (or on the region/scale data per triple), then the frozen
  interface's single fixed scaling/degreeBound under-specifies λ. The frozen
  interface may therefore be too weak/wrong for the paper statement.
- **Consequences:**
  - do not use the fixed-scaling S2604/S2603 P4 form as the paper P4;
  - do not close P4 via a uniform region-volume constant;
  - a correct P4 must expose the triple-dependent λ (or the correct
    scale/degree dependence) in the interface, and the region volume must be
    allowed to depend on it.
- **Status:** P4 remains open/refuted under the frozen fixed-scaling form;
  interface under-specification is a blocking design issue. No fake fix.

## 2026-11-06 — P4/P5 = ABC-equivalent core; frozen interface insufficient

- **P4/P5 conjunction is equivalent to an ABC-type height bound.** The combined
  P4/P5 dictionary/region statement is not a technical lemma: it is an
  ABC-equivalent core. Proving P4+P5 as currently shaped would amount to an
  ABC-type height inequality.
- **Fixed or triple-dependent scaling cannot bypass the growth condition.**
  Neither a single fixed scaling/degreeBound nor a per-triple λ removes the
  growth requirement; the unbounded arithmetic weight vs. controlled region
  volume forces a genuine growth/Θ-link input. A scaling choice alone is not a
  substitute for the estimate.
- **The frozen interface is insufficient to express the paper Θ-link estimate.**
  The current frozen `IQHullLogVolumeInterface`/fixed-scaling P4-P5 shape lacks
  the data needed for the paper's Θ-link estimate (triple-dependent λ, growth/
  log-volume comparison, and the correct signed normalization). It is
  under-specified for the paper statement, not merely inconvenient.
- **Label: P4/P5 = ABC-equivalent core.** Do not present P4/P5 as a routine
  closure step or as derivable from the frozen fixed-scale interface. Treat any
  claimed P4/P5 completion as requiring an ABC-strength input and audit it
  accordingly. No fake fix; P4/P5 remain open.

## 2026-11-07 — S2811P6 Prestack ACTUAL: presheafHom is P, and P is an etale sheaf

- S2811P6PrestackActual ACTUAL:
  src 6474 B SHA256 7A7BFBC3E86E7161A3C85369E50764BD512AF67E67691B1B3E602EC2E6BA143D;
  olean 176488 B SHA256 B2A0EBC05D2EABCC7C6F1332EBA2960557421EE03CCE56A3E3F0EE8DE3080062.
  Serial compile EXIT=0 with `lake env lean -j1 -R 'D:/lean' -o
  .lake/build/lib/lean/tmp/sheaf/xif/paper/S2811P6PrestackActual.olean
  tmp/sheaf/xif/paper/S2811P6PrestackActual.lean`; no errors, no warnings.
  All four `#print axioms` report exactly [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound];
  no sorry/admit/axiom in the source.
- Proved, unconditional, for F : Type u, [Field F], X S : SchemeOverField F:
  * `presheafHom_obj_eq`: for M N in the fibre of
    `schemeRepresentableEtalePseudofunctor F X` over S and T : (Over S)^op,
    `(…).presheafHom M N |>.obj T = (Discrete.mk (T.unop.hom ≫ M.as) ⟶
    Discrete.mk (T.unop.hom ≫ N.as))` (rfl);
  * `presheafHom_subsingleton`: that value is a subsingleton;
  * `presheafHomIso`: `presheafHom M N ≅ P F X S M.as N.as` (componentwise
    ULift/Subtype <-> equality; naturality and the iso laws are Subsingleton.elim
    after `ConcreteCategory.hom_ext`);
  * `P_isSheaf`: `Presheaf.IsSheaf ((etaleTopology F).over S) (P F X S m n)`;
  * `presheafHom_isSheaf` and the instance
    `schemeRepresentableEtalePseudofunctor_isPrestack :
     (schemeRepresentableEtalePseudofunctor F X).IsPrestack (etaleTopology F)`.
- Route for `P_isSheaf` (no input beyond S2811_yoneda_isSheaf): rewrite to
  `Presieve.IsSheaf`; for a covering sieve R on Y : Over S, every arrow
  f : Z ⟶ Y.left of the covering sieve `Sieve.overEquiv Y R` (which lies in
  `etaleTopology F Y.left` by the definition of the over-topology) gives the local
  equality `f ≫ (Y.hom ≫ m) = f ≫ (Y.hom ≫ n)` from the section `x (Over.homMk f)`;
  separatedness of `yoneda.obj X` (`Presieve.IsSheaf.isSeparated` +
  `IsSeparatedFor.ext`, not the full hom_ext) then yields the global equality
  `Y.hom ≫ m = Y.hom ≫ n`. Amalgamation and uniqueness are automatic because every
  value of P is a subsingleton. The empty-cover case is included in the same
  argument: `IsSheafFor` at the empty presieve forces the value of `yoneda.obj X` to
  be a subsingleton, so separatedness at ⊥ is genuine and still gives the equality.
- Implementation note: in this Mathlib (v4.32.2) the morphisms of `Type u` are the
  wrapped `TypeCat.Hom` (notation `↾f`, lemmas `types_comp_apply`, `types_id_apply`),
  not plain functions; hence the naturality/iso laws are stated through
  `ConcreteCategory.hom_ext`. `presheafHom_obj_eq` is by rfl and needs the object
  ascription `(... : Discrete (T.unop.left ⟶ X))` on the left-hand side.
- Consumer (G4): this closes the prestack half, i.e. descent of morphisms, for the
  represented Cat-valued pseudofunctor `schemeRepresentableEtalePseudofunctor F X`
  with respect to the big etale topology. `IsStack` still needs the effectiveness
  (objects) part, and the faithful D6 stack constructor is still missing.
- Checked separately by importing the olean in a temporary file (EXIT=0): the
  `IsPrestack` instance is synthesizable and `IsPrestack.isSheaf` applies to arbitrary
  S and M N; the temporary check file was removed afterwards.

## 2026-11-08 c3HaarLogVolume_smul_norm false; c3LogVolume_smul_norm actual

- Original statement `(haarLogVolume μ (u•S)).toReal = Real.log c + (haarLogVolume μ S).toReal` is FALSE without normalization: `haarLogVolume` uses `ENNReal.ofReal`, so `toReal` truncates negative logs. Counterexample: `μ S = 1/2`, `c = 1/2` gives LHS `0` but RHS `log(1/2) + 0 < 0`.
- Corrected theorem `c3LogVolume_smul_norm` uses real logs of `(μ ·).toReal`: `Real.log ((μ (u•S)).toReal) = Real.log c + Real.log ((μ S).toReal)`; proved in `S2733ScalingActual` using `S2733_scalingHaar_norm`, `ENNReal.toReal_mul`, `ENNReal.coe_toReal`, `Real.log_mul`.
- Verified: src BA51CDE2A2BE8259D671F079624DC272DAB30FA2DA2DD4CE79FB4130BDFA8F66, olean C837B7BF705676AF3649C1B6843BF2613783D2F48CCBE046FCAE08D3B47832FE, EXIT=0.

## 2026-11-09 S2726 per-place region closedness/compactness audit

- `S2726PerPlaceUpdateRegion rho` is defined by coordinate constraints `Real.log ‖y_j‖ ≤ rho i`.
- If `rho i < 0`, the coordinate set is `{x | 0 < ‖x‖ ≤ exp(rho i)}`: NOT closed (0 is a limit point but `Real.log 0 = 0 > rho i`). Counterexample: `rho i = -1`.
- Hence unconditional `IsClosed`/`IsCompact`/`hfinite` is FALSE; need hypothesis `hρ : ∀ i, 0 ≤ rho i`.
- Under `hρ`, constraint is equivalent to `‖x‖ ≤ exp(rho i)` (closed ball), so finite intersection is closed/bounded and compact in finite dimension.
- `hge1` is not derivable from compact/open alone; possible route: `hρ` ⇒ tensor lattice `TL ⊆ region`, plus Haar normalization `μ TL = 1` ⇒ `1 ≤ (μ region).toReal`.
- Status: closed/bounded/compact proofs NOT yet written or compiled (no olean).

## 2026-11-09 S2726 region is UNBOUNDED (support>=2 coordinates unconstrained)

- `FinitePadicTensorIndex M := (i : ι) → Fin (Module.finrank ℚ_[p] (M i))` is the full dependent function space.
- `S2726PerPlaceUpdateRegion rho` constrains only coordinates `Function.update defaultTensorIndex i k`, i.e. support at a single place i.
- Any coordinate with support at two distinct places `i ≠ j` is NOT constrained by any `rho`; scaling that coordinate arbitrarily keeps `y` in the region but makes the norm unbounded.
- Hence for `ι` with at least two elements (in particular C3.tensorIndex unless proved a subsingleton), the region is NOT bounded, NOT compact, and `hfinite` is FALSE unconditionally.
- What IS true: `isClosed_perPlaceUpdateRegion` under `hρ : ∀ i, 0 ≤ rho i` (proved, actual, S2743PerPlaceRegionClosedActual, src 91182C50A16E1CEB108A4CB2CBA386250F5D922447D42414F14B96F9F58F00B4).
- Correction needed: region should constrain ALL coordinates, e.g. all `y j` with product/sum bounds, or restrict to the subspace of support<=1 (which is finite-dimensional and compact for hρ), or use a different tensor region definition.
